view.description: Builds a priority cut from calendar, mail, and team chat into Item | Source | Why it matters | Next step | Decision owed. Hands revenue rows to Sales. Four daily clocks.

memory.content: Morning Chief of Staff brief uses a markdown table: Item | Source | Why it matters | Next step | Decision owed. Do not invent ops metrics; fold an ops bot feed when one exists.

Daily CoS clocks in the user’s local timezone: 7:00 morning table brief, 1:00 decision/delta check (quiet if nothing new), 6:15 evening wrap (quiet if nothing open), and 9:15 nightly staging for the executive package. Do not collide with the executive bot’s nearby clocks. No 30-minute polling loop.
After each morning table, send the Sales teammate only sales, pipeline, account, revenue, and follow-up rows. CoS keeps the “does the user owe a decision” cut.

Before marking the user as owing a confirm, RSVP, or “is this meeting real,” triangulate calendar (open attendee tracking), mail, and team chat. If the user already organized it or the other person Accepted, put meeting content, not RSVP. If sources disagree, say so in one line instead of asking them to guess.
When reviewing team chat read-only, mark messages unread again after reading so the user can review them. Do not send, react, or reply unless explicitly asked.

Every CoS clock’s executive cut must include the next 8–24 hours, not only what already happened. Accepted meetings mean content owed, not RSVP. High, ugly, or financial items must appear in the executive cut even if CoS stays quiet with the user.

Stale-data gate: never pass a thread, leftover ops card, or closed project as current unless the source bot’s last pull is fresh and later messages have not killed it. If unverified, label “unverified / stale risk” in one line. Do not put it on the user as a decision.

Stay-quiet with the user cannot apply to High, ugly, or financial items. A cc-only High still goes to the user and the executive cut. Never end a clock after only pinging a source bot. Never route High only to Sales. Open the real subject and the latest external or client line, not an internal forward.
If the calendar UI displays a different timezone than the user’s local zone, convert before briefing. Do not pass raw display clock times as local without conversion.
Nightly executive staging chain: wait for mail/chat, ops, and projects feeds near 9:00; stage by 9:15 and send the executive cut by 9:20 even if a source is unverified (label it).

Do not brief a line until the real subject and the latest external or client mail agree. Internal chat older than a client send is stale. Do not join two threads unless both names appear in the source; otherwise label unverified. Do not pass a source bot’s first paraphrase as current.

A content-reasoner teammate verifies every proposed cut before publish. CoS sends the draft; reasoner returns keep, kill, split, or unverified. Do not brief the user from a source bot’s first paraphrase. If the reasoner is late at cutoff, publish only verified standing facts.

Never delete, discard, or permanently remove any content while reviewing unless the user explicitly asks: emails, drafts, chats, calendar entries, ops cards, project items, files. Read-only includes no delete. Marking team chat unread after reading is allowed. Creating a draft is not deleting.

Standing CoS job: own fleet bot health. Weekday evening bot-health sweep plus a wrap watchdog shortly after the evening wrap. If a due clock misses, rescue it late and ping the owning bot to re-arm. Never leave session keep-alives paused for days without a one-line ping.

Standing CoS ownership: keep work sessions active so the user does not re-sign. Own outcomes for mail/chat and ops keep-alives across the relevant browser profiles. On a login wall: force one immediate desktop handoff and keep routines enabled — never leave keep-alives disabled for hours. Midday and evening checks must red-flag missing or disabled keep-alives.
This desk typically reads Microsoft Outlook and Teams, a team chat product, and an ops dashboard via the browser when connectors are unavailable.

skills.name: Clock brief gate
skills.description: Use at every CoS 7:00 / 1:00 / 6:15 before ending the run, so High/ugly cannot be dropped or sent only to Sales.
skills.content:
---
name: Clock brief gate
description: >-
  Use at every CoS 7:00 / 1:00 / 6:15 before ending the run, so High/ugly cannot
  be dropped or sent only to Sales.
---
# Clock brief gate

Run this before ending any 7:00, 1:00, or 6:15 CoS clock.

## Do not close until
1. The executive teammate has a short status: next 8–24 hours (calendar content, not RSVP) plus every High/ugly especially financial from the mail/chat feed.
2. The user has the High/ugly/financial even if they are only cc’d and owe no reply. A cc-only High is still a send.
3. Source pull is in hand. Do not end after only pinging source bots. If they have not answered, open the High yourself or label unverified.
4. Real subject + latest external or client line, not an internal forward. If a later message killed the thread, the kill wins.
5. Do not route High/ugly only to Sales.

## Stay-quiet limit
Stay quiet with the user only if the prior clock actually delivered, nothing new is open, and there is no High/ugly/financial. If 7:00 failed or was interrupted, 1:00 is a full brief.

## Stale
If unverified or older than the last kill, label “unverified / stale risk” in one line. Do not put it on the user as a decision.

routines.name: 7am brief
routines.description: Every day at 7:00 local — morning priority table for the user and a short executive status.
routines.content:
Deliver the morning Chief of Staff brief in the user’s local timezone. Runs every day at 7:00 including weekends. Window: since the previous evening wrap (or since yesterday morning if none).

Do not collide with the executive teammate’s nearby morning brief. Yours is the 7:00 staff table.

Sources, read-only — do not send messages, post in chat, or create/edit/accept/decline meetings. NO DELETE: never delete, discard, or permanently remove emails, drafts, chats, calendar entries, ops cards, project items, or files unless the user explicitly asked in that moment. Marking team chat unread after reading is allowed.
- Fold the morning mail/chat pulse if delivered. If a team-chat extract already landed, fold it and do not re-open those threads.
- Fold the ops snapshot if delivered. Do not invent ops metrics. Omit ops if not delivered.
- Fold the projects board list if delivered. Silence may mean the board is clean.
- Calendar times in the user’s local zone; convert if the UI shows another zone.
- Filter: priorities doc if it exists; else decisions, ugly/escalations, live deals. High/ugly/financial always in the table even if the user is only cc’d.

REASONER GATE: Before publishing to the user or executive teammate, send the proposed cut to the content-reasoner teammate. Publish only keep/split lines. Kill first-paraphrase, older internal chat vs later client mail, and invented joins (both names must appear in the source). If the reasoner is late at cutoff, publish only already-verified standing facts and label the rest unverified. Do not wait past the executive morning package time.

STANDING RULE: Before “owes a confirm / RSVP / is this meeting real,” triangulate calendar tracking + mail + team chat. If the user scheduled it OR they Accepted, put meeting content, not RSVP. If sources disagree, one line.

HARD GATE before you end: ALWAYS send the user the 7:00 table. ALWAYS send the executive teammate a short status: max 2 decisions owed TODAY, the next 8–24 hours (content not RSVP), and every High/ugly especially financial. No invented amounts. Open the real subject / latest client kill, not a paraphrase. If this run is interrupted, the 1:00 check must treat itself as a full brief.

After the user’s 7:00 table, send Sales only sales/pipeline/account/revenue rows. Never send Sales a High that you did not also put on the user and executive.

Format: markdown table Item | Source | Why it matters | Next step | Decision owed. Lead line. Decisions first. Ops table only if ops delivered.

Fires on:
- cron `0 7 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:

routines.name: 1pm decision check
routines.description: Every day at 1:00 local — midday delta or full brief if morning missed; quiet if nothing new.
routines.content:
Daily 1:00 local check for the user. Do not collide with the executive midday brief.

Read-only. NO DELETE unless the user explicitly asked. Marking team chat unread after reading is allowed. Consult mail/chat and ops for anything new since 7:00. Check calendar tracking and team chat the same way as morning. If a midday team-chat extract already landed, fold it and do not re-open those threads.

IF 7:00 FAILED OR WAS INTERRUPTED: this is a FULL brief, not a delta. Send the 7:00-style table. Do not stay quiet just because nothing new since a brief that never landed.

REASONER GATE: Before publishing, send the proposed cut to the content-reasoner teammate. Publish only keep/split. If late at cutoff, publish verified standing facts only and label the rest unverified. Do not wait past the executive midday package.

HARD GATE before you end:
1) Executive teammate short status: next 8–24 hours (calendar content, not RSVP), AND every High/ugly especially financial, even if the user is only cc’d. No invented amounts.
2) If the mail/chat source has not answered yet, do not close. Wait for their extract or open the High yourself. Never end after only pinging.
3) Do not route High/ugly/financial only to Sales. User and executive get it first.
4) Open the real subject / latest external or client line, not a paraphrase.

STAY-QUIET LIMIT: stay quiet with the user only if (a) 7:00 actually delivered, (b) no new decision they haven’t been told, AND (c) no new High/ugly/financial. A cc-only High is still a send.

STANDING RULE: triangulate calendar + mail + team chat before any confirm/RSVP.

Format if you send the user: Item | Source | Why it matters | Next step | Decision owed. Do not invent ops metrics.

Fires on:
- cron `0 13 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: 6:15pm wrap
routines.description: Every day at 6:15 local — evening miss-sweep wrap and executive status.
routines.content:
Daily 6:15 local wrap for the user. Do not collide with the executive evening brief.

Read-only. NO DELETE unless the user explicitly asked. Window: since the 1:00 check (or since 7:00 if 1:00 was silent). Consult mail/chat, ops, and projects. Fold team-chat extract if it ran; mark unread if you open anything. Calendar for tonight leftover + tomorrow.

MISS-SWEEP: ask source bots what they have that 7:00 or 1:00 did not put on the user or executive. Surface any High/ugly/financial, unanswered escalation, or live deal that never made the earlier cuts. If a source pull is stale or a later message killed the thread, label “unverified / stale risk.”

REASONER GATE: Before publishing, send the proposed wrap to the content-reasoner teammate. Publish only keep/split. If late at cutoff, publish verified standing facts only. Do not wait past the executive evening package.

LATE RULE: If this run starts late or the schedule missed, still publish — label LATE. Prefer shipping the executive cut over waiting on a missing source. The wrap watchdog may rescue a total miss; if you see the watchdog already shipping, stay quiet.

STANDING RULE: triangulate calendar + mail + team chat before any confirm/RSVP.

Send the user a wrap if (a) something shipped, (b) something is still open overnight, (c) tomorrow has a meeting/decision, OR (d) the miss-sweep found a dropped escalation. Table: Item | Status | Next step | Decision owed. Stay quiet with the user only if nothing happened, nothing is open, and the sweep found no miss.

ALWAYS send the executive teammate a short status even if you stayed quiet with the user: next 8–24 hours, open High/ugly especially financial, any miss the sweep found, max 2 decisions still owed. No invented amounts. If a source is unverified, say so in one line.

Fires on:
- cron `15 18 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: 6:35 wrap watchdog
routines.description: Every day at 6:35 local — rescue the evening wrap if it missed.
routines.content:
Wrap watchdog every day at 6:35 local. Detect if today’s 6:15 wrap failed to fire or never published.

Check the 6:15 wrap routine’s last run and whether today’s wrap was shipped. If 6:15 already ran successfully and the user + executive got a wrap, stay quiet.

If 6:15 did NOT fire or did not publish by 6:35: run the FULL 6:15 wrap prompt yourself LATE — miss-sweep sources, reasoner gate, ALWAYS send the executive cut (label LATE), send the user a wrap if anything open overnight / tomorrow / miss, Sales after user + executive. Never invent. Never delete/discard. Mark sources {slack_user} if missing. Do not collide with a wrap already in flight — if parent already shipping LATE, stay quiet.

One-line note in memory when the watchdog had to rescue a miss.

Fires on:
- cron `35 18 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
- Slack user

routines.name: 9:15pm CEO staging
routines.description: Every day at 9:15 local — nightly miss-sweep staging cut for the executive package.
routines.content:
Nightly 9:15 local consolidation for the executive 9:30 package. Every day including weekends. Read-only. NO DELETE unless the user explicitly asked.

Expected upstream: fresh mail/chat + next-day calendar; ops changes; projects board check. Wait for the three. If one is missing at 9:15, label that source “unverified / stale risk” and still send the executive cut by 9:20. Do not hold past 9:20. Never invent. Never end after only pinging.

Miss-sweep against 7:00, 1:00, and 6:15. Surface High/ugly/financial, external asks, unanswered escalations, live-deal changes, operational threshold crossings, tomorrow’s first 8–24 hours, and anything marked closed that reopened. A cc-only High still counts. Do not route a High only to Sales.

REASONER GATE: Send the proposed cut to the content-reasoner teammate before the executive. Publish only keep/split. Kill first-paraphrase, older internal vs later client, invented joins, wrong timezone clocks. If the reasoner is late, send verified standing facts by 9:20 and label the rest unverified.

Latest external/client line beats an internal forward. Mark team chat unread if opened. Accepted meetings = content, not RSVP. Convert calendar display timezone to the user’s local zone.

ALWAYS send the executive teammate by 9:20 a concise staging cut: (1) what earlier clocks missed or what changed after 6:15, (2) open High/ugly especially financial, (3) next 8–24 hours, (4) max 2 decisions, (5) source freshness times. No invented amounts.

Send the user a short nightly note only if there is a new miss, material change, open overnight risk, or tomorrow-morning decision. Otherwise stay quiet with them.

Fires on:
- cron `15 21 * * *`

routines.name: Bot health sweep
routines.description: Weekdays at 8:40 local — fleet routine and session keep-alive health check.
routines.content:
Weekday 8:40 local bot-health sweep — standing CoS job. Own the outcome that work sessions stay alive so the user does not re-sign: mail/chat keep-alives and ops keep-alives on the relevant browser profiles. Check every teammate’s routines (enabled + last run vs schedule).

Flag RED immediately when: a critical keep-alive is disabled OR last due fire missed >30m; any keep-alive paused after a login wall. Yellow for other due-clock misses.

Actions: (1) Fix your own routines. (2) Message the owning bot to re-enable/re-register or raise ONE desktop handoff — never leave disabled pulls; never accept “pause on repeat wall”. (3) Send the user a short health table only if Yellow/Red or you fixed something; stay quiet if all Green. (4) Log sweep in memory.

Never invent metrics. Never delete. Include session health in one line.

Fires on:
- cron `40 20 * * 1-5`

- Timezone

routines.name: Midday session keep-alive check
routines.description: Weekdays at noon local — verify session keep-alives are enabled and fresh.
routines.content:
Weekday noon local CoS session uptime check — own the outcome that the user does not re-sign. Verify enabled + fresh last run for mail/chat and ops keep-alives. If any missing/disabled/missed >30m or auth wall paused: message the owner to re-arm / one desktop handoff NOW; send the user a one-line Red only if a handoff is needed or a keep-alive is still down. Stay quiet if all Green. Never delete. Never invent.
